questions.q: Salt water is an example of a mixture. Define a mixture.
choices: substances that always form new products
substances that are not chemically combined
questions.explain: A mixture is made of substances that are not chemically combined. They can be separated by physical methods, such as evaporating salt water.

questions.q: A tea strainer removes tea leaves from tea. Name the separation technique used.
questions.explain: The strainer lets the liquid tea through and holds back the solid tea leaves. This is filtration.

questions.q: Salt water is heated until only salt is left. Name this separation technique.
questions.explain: Heating the salt water drives off the water as steam and leaves the salt behind. This is evaporation.

questions.q: Coloured sweets contain several dyes. Name the technique that separates these dyes.
questions.explain: Paper chromatography separates a mixture of dyes. Each dye travels a different distance up the paper.

questions.q: A mixture is stirred in water and then filtered. Identify the mixture this separates.
questions.explain: Salt dissolves in water but sand does not. Filtering holds back the sand and lets the salt solution through.

questions.q: Distillation is used on seawater. Name the substance collected.
questions.explain: Distillation boils the seawater and cools the steam back into a liquid. The liquid collected is pure water. The salt stays behind.

questions.q: Sugar dissolves in water to make a solution. Identify the role of the water.
questions.explain: The water dissolves the sugar, so the water is the solvent. The sugar is the solute.

questions.q: A mixture of sand and water is filtered. Name the solid left on the filter paper.
questions.explain: The solid left on the filter paper is called the residue. Here the residue is sand.

questions.q: A mixture of sand and water is filtered. Name the liquid that passes through.
questions.explain: The liquid that passes through the filter paper is called the filtrate. Here the filtrate is water.

questions.q: A food colouring gives three spots on chromatography paper. Identify what it is.
questions.explain: Each spot on the chromatogram is a different dye. Three spots show the food colouring is a mixture of three dyes.

questions.q: A pure food colouring is tested by paper chromatography. Predict the number of spots.
questions.explain: A pure substance contains only one dye. So it gives only one spot on the chromatogram.

questions.q: Dyes move up chromatography paper with the solvent. Identify the dye that moves furthest.
questions.explain: A dye that dissolves well in the solvent is carried furthest up the paper. So the most soluble dye moves furthest.

questions.q: Food M gives a spot level with banned dye A. Identify what M contains.
questions.explain: A spot at the same height as a known dye is that dye. So food M contains banned dye A.

questions.q: Cooking and burning are examples of chemical reactions. Define a chemical reaction.
choices: a process where a liquid evaporates
a process where a solid dissolves
a process where new products form
a process that separates a mixture
questions.explain: In a chemical reaction new products are formed. Cooking and burning both make new substances.

questions.q: An iron nail rusts. State the two things needed for rusting.
questions.explain: Iron rusts only when both water and oxygen are present. Without either one, the nail does not rust.

questions.q: Blue litmus paper is dipped into an acid. Describe its colour change.
questions.explain: Acids turn blue litmus paper red. Alkalis turn red litmus paper blue.

questions.q: Detergent solution is alkaline. State one property of alkalis.
questions.explain: Alkalis turn red litmus paper blue and have a pH above 7. Acids taste sour and turn blue litmus red.

questions.q: Neutral solutions are neither acidic nor alkaline. State the pH of a neutral solution.
questions.explain: A neutral solution has a pH of exactly 7. Pure water is neutral.

questions.q: Lemon juice tastes sour. Identify the pH of lemon juice.
questions.explain: Lemon juice tastes sour because it is acidic. Acids have a pH less than 7.

questions.q: Solutions have pH 2, 5, 7 and 12. Identify the pH of the most acidic one.
questions.explain: The lower the pH, the more acidic the solution. pH 2 is the lowest, so it is the most acidic.

questions.q: A solution has a pH of 12. Identify the type of solution.
questions.explain: A pH above 7 means the solution is alkaline. So a pH of 12 is alkaline.

questions.q: Universal indicator turns red in a solution. Identify the solution.
questions.explain: Universal indicator turns red in a strong acid. Dilute sulphuric acid is an acid. Ammonia and sodium hydroxide are alkalis, and distilled water is neutral.

questions.q: An acid reacts with a metal. State the products of this reaction.
questions.explain: An acid reacts with a metal to give a salt and hydrogen gas. The hydrogen can be seen as bubbles.

questions.q: An acid reacts with a carbonate. State the products of this reaction.
questions.explain: An acid reacts with a carbonate to give a salt, carbon dioxide and water. The carbon dioxide can be seen as bubbles.

questions.q: Magnesium metal is added to lemon juice. Name the gas given off.
questions.explain: Lemon juice is acidic. An acid reacts with a metal such as magnesium to give a salt and hydrogen gas.

questions.q: Egg shells contain a carbonate. They are added to vinegar. Name the gas given off.
questions.explain: Vinegar is an acid. An acid reacts with a carbonate to give a salt, water and carbon dioxide gas.

questions.q: A gas puts out a lighted splint with a pop sound. Identify the gas.
questions.explain: Hydrogen puts out a lighted splint with a 'pop' sound. This is the test for hydrogen.

questions.q: A gas is bubbled into limewater and turns it chalky. Identify the gas.
questions.explain: Carbon dioxide turns limewater chalky (milky). This is the test for carbon dioxide.

questions.q: A reaction makes a salt and hydrogen gas. Identify the two reactants.
questions.explain: An acid reacts with a metal to give a salt and hydrogen. An acid and a carbonate give carbon dioxide instead, and an acid and a base give water.

questions.q: Neutralisation is a reaction between an acid and a base. State the products.
questions.explain: In neutralisation an acid reacts with a base to give a salt and water.

questions.q: Too much stomach acid causes indigestion. Identify the type of substance in antacid medicine.
questions.explain: Antacids contain a base. The base neutralises the extra stomach acid and eases the indigestion.

questions.q: Toothpaste neutralises acid on the teeth. Identify the type of substance in toothpaste.
questions.explain: Toothpaste contains a mild base. It neutralises the acid that bacteria make on our teeth.

questions.q: Fabric softener neutralises alkaline detergent in laundry. Identify the type of substance in it.
questions.explain: Fabric softener contains a mild acid. The acid neutralises the alkaline detergent left in the laundry.

questions.q: Soil is too acidic for crops. Name the substance farmers add to neutralise it.
questions.explain: Calcium hydroxide is a base. It neutralises the acid in the soil so that crops can grow well.

questions.q: Calcium hydroxide is added to acidic soil. Name this type of reaction.
questions.explain: Calcium hydroxide is a base and the soil is acidic. A base reacting with an acid is neutralisation.

questions.q: Some detergents contain phosphates. Predict what phosphates cause in rivers.
questions.explain: Phosphates are nutrients for algae. When they wash into rivers, algae grow very quickly and cause an algal bloom.

questions.q: A thick layer of algae covers a river. State what happens to the oxygen level.
choices: it rises and then stays high
questions.explain: The algae block sunlight, so water plants below cannot photosynthesise. When the algae die, bacteria rot them and use up oxygen. So the oxygen level decreases.

questions.q: Microbes break down waste in waste water. Name the microbes used.
questions.explain: Bacteria break down the waste in waste water. They are used at water treatment plants.
